clue.text: Colleague in middle of room keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping says the middle letters hold the next piece within them
takes the letters of room inside its two ends, dropping the first and last

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A workmate in the middle of the room is staying very hushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal slang for a counterpart or partner at work.

clue.text: Bring an end to anger through teasing

definitions.meaning: to conclude or finish off a meeting or business
to rile someone by taking a rise out of them

explanation.surface: Stopping a quarrel that started when someone was mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: to conclude proceedings, and to provoke someone with a prank.

clue.text: Stuff like food that can be served again

definitions.text: Stuff like food that can be served again

parts.words: Stuff like food that can be served again
parts.note: leftovers can be served a second time; also food said to repeat on you comes back up

explanation.surface: Leftovers fit for another meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to be done or given a second time; food that repeats on you returns as indigestion.

clue.text: Excited men turning up to be given employment

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word for men is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
something given employment has been put to use

explanation.surface: Staff are thrilled to arrive and find they have jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused means stirred up or agitated, a near synonym for being excited.

clue.text: Protected with a 'nutcase' around?

parts.note: a nutcase is jokingly a case for the nut, or head: a protective hat worn round it

explanation.surface: Kept safe while some lunatic is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing protective headgear, the casing for the head that slang calls the nut.

clue.text: Refuse from crowd building up

indicators.note: in a down clue building up means the verb for crowd is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to cram is to crowd or pack tightly

explanation.surface: Rubbish piling up as a mob gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the residue of grapes or other fruit left after pressing, i.e. waste matter.

clue.text: Put new energy into troubled lives — one gets little thanks getting involved

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of lives are disturbed into a new order
one gets says the numeral is added to the letters being stirred, joining the pool
getting involved says the numeral and the short thanks are mixed in among those letters

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
ta is a short, informal British word of thanks

explanation.surface: Reviving troubled lives, someone receives barely any gratitude for interfering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' stirs the letters of lives, and 'getting involved' brings the numeral and the short thanks into that mix; the thanks lands whole inside, after VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitalise is to invigorate or fill with life and vigour.

clue.text: More than one scientist gets to go round island following old account

indicators.note: to go round says the word gets surrounds the remaining pieces
following says the island comes after the old account

parts.note: a log is a record or account of events

explanation.surface: Someone touring an island after reading an old travel record.
explanation.definitionFit: These scientists study rocks and the earth's structure; the plural matches more than one.

clue.text: Demure English principal

parts.note: prim means demure and proper

explanation.surface: A modest English headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like a noun for a head of school, but here it is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime and principal are synonyms meaning main or chief.

clue.text: Crucial time I have after event at Sadler's Wells, maybe

indicators.note: after puts the time and I have behind the stage performance

parts.note: Sadler's Wells is a London theatre for opera and dance, so an opera is one event there
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone insists their schedule after a London show is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadler's Wells is a theatre in London known for opera and dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The operative factor is the key or significant one, so operative can mean crucial.

clue.text: Strange quality that lucky and unlucky numbers have?

definitions.meaning: peculiarity or weirdness as a trait

definitions.text: that lucky and unlucky numbers have?
definitions.meaning: seven, lucky, and thirteen, unlucky, are both not divisible by two

explanation.surface: Musing on the peculiar character of superstitious numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means peculiarity, and also the property of a whole number not divisible by two.

clue.text: Divine messenger's strange email gripping church

indicators.note: gripping says the jumbled letters clasp the church abbreviation between them
strange says the letters of email are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: An angel's odd email that clutches at religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'messenger's' stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is one of the archangels, and angels are by origin heavenly messengers.

clue.text: Agent wants old books put in new container

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
OT, the Old Testament, is the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sales agent needs his old books moved to fresh packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant into a fresh or larger pot.

clue.text: How to get a goat to sleep? Music!

definitions.text: How to get a goat to sleep?
definitions.meaning: lull a male goat by swaying it
a fusion of early rock and roll with country hillbilly style

explanation.surface: A silly question about lulling livestock, answered with a musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockabilly is a 1950s American style of popular song mixing rock and country.

clue.text: Providing precise information on action to blind mice?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the tails of three blind mice

explanation.surface: Instructions on what to do with sightless rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Blind Mice is a nursery rhyme in which the farmer's wife cuts off their tails with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Detailing means itemising; read as de-tailing it means removing tails.

clue.text: Divine act, I fancy, is typical

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imagining that an act of God is quite normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indicative of something means being characteristic or representative of it.

clue.text: The insensibility that a crocodile has?

definitions.text: The insensibility that a crocodile has?

parts.words: The insensibility that a crocodile has?
parts.note: reptiles are literally of low body temperature, and figuratively this means callous lack of feeling

explanation.surface: Wondering about the reptile's heartless nature.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means callous ruthlessness, and literally describes animals whose temperature depends on surroundings.

clue.text: Son (10) enthralled by foreign song — he did this?

definitions.text: Son (10) enthralled by foreign song — he did this?

indicators.note: enthralled by says the son and the number are held within the song

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
the number ten written as a word

explanation.surface: A boy of ten captivated by a German song paid attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lied is a German song (as by Schubert); the whole clue also describes the rapt son.
explanation.definitionFit: A son held captive by a song would have paid attention to it, the act described.

clue.text: Old poetry, lines put out with too much hype?

definitions.text: put out with too much hype?

parts.note: verse is poetry
L is line, and LL is lines

explanation.surface: Ancient verse released with excessive publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversell is to promote or praise something more than it merits.

clue.text: Most severe state sure to be troublesome

indicators.note: letters that are troublesome are unruly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The harshest regime is certain to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerest is the superlative of austere, meaning stern, harsh or severe.

clue.text: Projects worth millions finally abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of worth are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of millions

explanation.surface: Schemes worth a fortune are eventually scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something can mean to hurl or cast it, the same as tossing.

clue.text: Last bit of food eaten by dogs — soft stuff

indicators.note: eaten by says the letter goes inside the dogs

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of food

explanation.surface: The dogs wolf the scraps of a meal, leaving something squishy.
explanation.definitionFit: Curdled milk forms soft white lumps, a soft substance used to make cheese.

clue.text: Artist sitting on bank on very few occasions

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on puts the artist above the next piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
to bank, as in bank on, is to depend or count on

explanation.surface: A painter perched on a riverbank, which happens seldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on hardly any occasions.

clue.text: Very cold types in top positions

definitions.text: Very cold types in top positions

parts.note: ice is very cold, as in ice-cold
capitals, or caps, are letters (type) used at the start of sentences and names

explanation.surface: Aloof, frosty people who hold senior posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the frozen masses that sit at the top of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar caps of permanent ice sit at the top and bottom of the globe.

clue.text: A vessel not properly closed?

parts.note: a jar is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A container whose lid isn't on tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is ajar, not fully shut.

clue.text: About to go to Scottish island as one out of the rat race?

definitions.text: one out of the rat race?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone escaping the daily grind by moving to a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has stopped working has left the competitive struggle of employment.

clue.text: Not all appreciated a mouldy cheese

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Few people like a cheese that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese usually sold in a red wax coating.

clue.text: Gladly given permit to remain unproductive

parts.note: lief is an archaic word meaning gladly or willingly
to allow is to permit

explanation.surface: Happily granted leave to do nothing useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland left unsown for a season to recover yields no crop, so stays idle.

clue.text: Electrical unit established by a lake in Africa

parts.note: the volt is the unit of electric potential

explanation.surface: A power measurement set up beside an African lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the world's largest reservoirs.
